speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me your age and if you have any history of head trauma, recent infections, or substance use? Also, have you experienced any neck stiffness or sensitivity to light?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given your history of taking haloperidol and the presence of fever and altered mentation, I need to assess for potential side effects. Do you have any muscle rigidity, excessive sweating, or rapid heart rate?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The combination of fever, altered mentation, generalized rigidity, and autonomic instability (profuse sweating) in a patient taking haloperidol is highly suggestive of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome.
